This page shows how to use the orange brick separator tool, with a QR code. It has no building step, so no pieces are added. The separator is not in the parts list, so I did not record it.
Step 1: a black 2x2 plate (b1) is the first piece.
Step 2: a black 1x6 plate (b2) is placed on b1. It hangs out sideways, with one end on the 2x2 plate. I could not tell from the small picture how many studs overlap, but it rests only on b1.
The overview picture at the top left shows the finished Sydney skyline model.
Step 3: a second black 2x2 plate (b3) goes at the same level as b1, beside it. The 1x6 plate b2 bridges b1 and b3 from above.
b3 goes under the already-placed b2, so it clutches nothing below it and rests_on is []. I could not edit b2's earlier entry, so I recorded the b2-on-b3 link as an other_join.
The picture is small, so the exact stud offsets are my best reading.
Step 4: a black 2x6 plate (b4) is added to the base, over the two 2x2 plates b1 and b3.
Step 5: a second black 2x6 plate (b5) is added, shifted sideways from b4 so the two overlap in a staggered layout. I read it as resting on b4 and on the 1x6 plate b2.
The pictures are small and the stud offsets are hard to read, so the exact rests_on lists for b4 and b5 are my best reading.
Step 6 (2x): two black 2x2 plates with two studs on the side (b6, b7) are added side by side at the right end of the base. Their side studs face the front.
I read both as sitting on the exposed studs at the end of the lower 2x6 plate b4. The picture is small, so this is my best reading.
Step 7: a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b8) is added at the front of the base, with its side studs facing front.
Step 8: a black 1x6 plate (b9) is added along the back edge, overhanging to the left.
The pictures are small, so the rests_on lists for b8 and b9 are my best reading of the layout.
Step 9: a black 2x6 plate (b10) is added at the left end of the base. It makes that end two studs wide.
The picture is small. I read it as a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795), not the one with side studs, and as resting on b9 and b4. This is my best reading.
Step 10: one more black 2x6 plate (b11) is added toward the right and back of the base.
The picture is small. The parts-list counts show it is a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795), because the 2x6 plates with side studs (lego-87609) did not drop. The rests_on list (b5, b8) is my best reading.
Step 11 (2x): two black 1x1 plates are added. The arrows point at one stud on the left plate (b10) and one stud toward the middle of the front of the base (b8).
The picture is small, so the exact studs they sit on are my best reading.
Step 12: a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b14) is added at the front-left of the base, with its side studs facing front.
I read it as resting on the left plate b10 and the 1x1 plate b12. The picture is small, so this is my best reading.

Step 13: a black 1x6 plate (b15) is added along the back-left edge, overhanging to the left. Two Dark Blue 1x2 plates (b16, b17) are placed on the middle of the base, as the first coloured pieces for the tower footprint.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.
Step 14: a black 6x6 plate (b18) is added at the left end of the base, forming the base of the tower area.
The picture is small, so which plates it sits on (b10, b14, b15) is my best reading.
Step 15: a black 2x6 plate (b19) is added next to the 6x6 plate, on the left part of the base.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b18, b14) is my best reading. I took it as a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795) from the box icon.
Step 16: a black 1x6 plate (b20) is added along the back-left edge, sticking out to the left.
The picture is small. I read it as resting on b19, but I am not sure which plates it clutches.
Step 17: a second black 6x6 plate (b21) is added at the left end, widening the base on that side.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b18, b19, b20) is my best reading.
Step 18: a black 1x4 plate (b22) and a black 2x6 plate (b23) are added on the left end of the base.
The pictures are small, so where they sit is my best reading. The 2x6 shape in the box is black, and the parts list has no black 2x4, so I used a 2x6 plate (lego-3795).

Earlier, the parts-list counts after step 13 dropped White 1x2 plates (lego-3023) by 2 and left Dark Blue 1x2 unchanged. The picture showed blue plates, so I recorded b16 and b17 as Dark Blue. The colour of b16 and b17 may need checking.

Step 19 is a separate sub-assembly, built off the main base, and it will be attached to it later. The parts box lists a black 2x6 plate, a 1x6 plate, two 2x2 plates and two 2x2 plates with side studs. Only sub-steps 1 and 2 are on this page.
Sub-step 1: a black 2x2 plate (b24) is the first piece of the sub-assembly.
Sub-step 2: a black 1x6 plate (b25) is put on b24, overhanging to one side, the same way as b1 and b2 at the start.
The other parts in the box (2x6 plate, second 2x2 plate, two plates with side studs) are not placed on this page.

Sub-step 3: a second black 2x2 plate (b26) goes beside b24, under the 1x6 plate b25. It clutches nothing below, so rests_on is [] and the link to b25 is recorded as an other_join. This repeats steps 1-3 of the main build (b1, b2, b3).
Sub-step 4: a black 2x6 plate (b27) goes on top.
Sub-step 5 (2x): two black 2x2 plates with two studs on the side (b28, b29) are added at the front, side studs facing front.
The pictures are small, so the exact rests_on for b27, b28 and b29 are my best reading.
No new pieces on this page. The arrow shows the finished step 19 sub-assembly (b24, b25, b26, b27, b28, b29) being attached to the left end of the base.
The picture is small, so I could not tell exactly which base plates it clutches. I recorded one join (b27 with b21) to show the attachment. The sub-assembly may also clutch b23 and b18.
Step 20: a black 1x6 plate (b30), a black 1x4 plate (b31) and a Dark Blue 1x2 plate (b32) are added on the left part of the base, over the join with the step 19 sub-assembly.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of where they sit.
The parts list shows 1x6 plates dropping from 1 to 0 after this step and 1x4 plates dropping from 7 to 6, which matches b30 and b31.

Step 21 (2x): two black 1x4 plates (b33, b34) are added. Each sticks out sideways to the front of the base, turned so its long side runs front-to-back. One is at the left near the blue plate and one is toward the middle.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.

The parts-list counts dropped White 1x2 plates (lego-3023) again, 5 to 4, after step 20. That suggests the blue-looking 1x2 plates in steps 13 and 20 are counted as White in the inventory, not Dark Blue. I recorded them as Dark Blue from the picture, so b16, b17 and b32 may need checking.

Step 22 (2x): two black 2x6 plates with 4 side studs (b35, b36) are laid side by side across the front of the base, with their side studs facing front. They are held on the two 1x4 plates (b33, b34) from step 21 that stick out to the front.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.
Step 23: a Tan 2x4 tile with groove (b37) is laid on top of the front 2x6 plates b35 and b36. It spans both of them.
The picture is small, so exactly which studs it covers is my best reading.

Step 24: two black 1x8 tiles (b38, b39) and one black 1x4 tile (b40) are pressed sideways onto the rows of side studs along the front of the base. They rest on nothing from below, so rests_on is [] and the joins are recorded as other_joins.
Each 1x8 tile fits one group of 8 side studs: b8 + b6 + b7 on the right front, and b14 + b28 + b29 on the left front. The 1x4 tile fits the 4 side studs of b36.
The picture is small and I could not see exactly which side-stud rows are covered, so the joins are my best reading.
Step 25 is a small separate sub-assembly: the black 1x8 tile printed with 'Sydney', held on two black 1x4 plates. It will be attached to the base later.
Sub-step 1: a black 1x4 plate (b41) is the first piece.
Sub-step 2: the Sydney-print 1x8 tile (b42) is put on b41, with the tile sticking out to the left.
Sub-step 3: the second 1x4 plate (b43) is pushed up from below under the left end of the tile b42 (red arrows). b43 clutches nothing below it, so rests_on is [] and its link to b42 is an other_join.
No new pieces on this page. The arrow shows the finished Sydney name-plate sub-assembly (b41, b42, b43) being pressed sideways onto the side studs along the front of the base.
The two 1x4 plates in the sub-assembly line up with the side studs of the two front 2x6 plates b35 and b36. The tile covers them, so the 'Sydney' print faces front.
The picture is small, so which plate meets which is my best reading.
Step 26: a black 1x4 tile with groove (b44) is pressed sideways onto the left-front side studs. It rests on nothing from below, so rests_on is [] and the join is an other_join.
The picture is small. I took the studs it covers to be the 4 side studs of b14. The earlier step 24 tile b39 may cover a different set of studs than I recorded.
Step 27: a Dark Green 1x4 tile with groove (b45) is placed at the far right end of the base, on the back right corner. It is the first of the green pieces for the grass at the bridge end.
The picture is small, so which plates it covers (b11, b7) is my best reading.

Step 28: four Dark Green 1x1 tiles (b46-b49) go next to the green 1x4 tile b45 at the right end, to make a small grass area. A Tan 1x1 plate (b50) and a Tan 1x3 brick (b51) go beside it, as the base of the bridge tower.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of which base plates each piece sits on.

My earlier notes about colour mismatches were wrong. The unplaced-parts list seems to count down by part type, taking the first colour listed. So the colours I read from the pictures (blue, green, black) stay as recorded.
Step 29 (2x): two Dark Tan 1x2 tiles with groove (b52, b53) are placed at the right end of the base, next to the green tiles and the tan brick, to make the path or ground there.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.

Step 30: 31 Trans-Light Blue 1x2 tiles (b54-b84) cover the top of the base from the tan tile to the green and tan area at the right end, forming the harbour water. Two White 1x2 tiles with two vertical teeth (b85, b86) stand in the water as small sails.
The water tiles are in a strip about two studs wide, and the tiles have no studs, so nothing sits on top of them. The sail tiles therefore clutch base plates directly, in gaps left in the water.
The picture is small and the 31 tiles cover many plates, so the rests_on lists are only a rough guide, in order from left to right across the water. The count of 31 tiles and 2 sails is certain.
Step 31: two Dark Green 1x1 tiles (b87, b88) and a Tan 1x1 plate (b89) are added at the back-left end of the water strip, to make a small green bank with a stud for later pieces.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of which plates they sit on.

Step 32: a Tan 1x3 brick (b90) is placed at the back-left end of the water strip. It sits on the Tan 1x1 plate b89 and on the base plate b4 beside it. It matches the tan brick at the right end (b51), the bridge towers.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list is my best reading.

Step 33: the left end of the base (the tower and Opera House ground) is covered with 4 Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tiles, 11 Light Bluish Gray 1x2 jumper plates (one stud each, showing as black dots) and 1 Tan 1x2 tile (b95) next to the tan brick b90.

The picture is small and these pieces cover many plates, so the rests_on lists are a rough guess based on the left-end base plates (b18, b19, b21, b23, b27, b30-b32, b10). The counts and types are certain.

Step 34 (2x): a small sub-assembly is built twice. A black 1x1 plate is pushed up into a black inverted 2x1 slope (the red arrow). One copy goes at the left tan brick (b90) tower and one at the right tan brick (b51) tower, as the bridge tower caps.
Copy 1 is b107 (plate) with b108 (slope), at the left end. Copy 2 is b109 (plate) with b110 (slope), at the right end.
The picture is small, so which base plate each 1x1 plate sits on and which stud the slope shares with the tan brick are my best reading.

Step 35 (2x): two Tan 1x1 plates are stacked (one on the other, red arrow), and the stack is placed on a tower brick. One stack goes on the left tan brick b90 (b111, b112). The other goes on the right tan brick b51 (b113, b114), raising each tower by two plates.
The picture is small, so which stud of each brick the stack sits on is my best reading.
Step 36 starts a new separate sub-assembly, the Sydney Harbour Bridge arch (shown in the top picture). It is built off the base and attached later.
A black 1x10 plate (b115) is the first piece. A black 1x1 plate (b116) is pressed onto its right-end stud (red arrow).
Step 37: a black 1x4 plate (b117) is added on the right half of the 1x10 plate b115, next to the 1x1 plate b116 at the end.
Step 38: another black 1x10 plate (b118) goes on top of the right part of the arch, over b117, b116 and b115. It reaches past the right end of b115, lengthening the bridge deck.
The pictures are small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.
Step 39: the last black 1x10 plate (b119) is added to the bridge deck. It overlaps b118 and b115 and makes the deck longer.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b118, b115) is my best reading.
Step 40: a black 1x1 plate (b120) is pressed onto the left-end stud of the bridge deck (red arrow). A black 1x4 plate (b121), the last one, is added on the deck near that end.
The picture only shows the 1x1 plate arrow, so where the 1x4 plate goes is my best reading from the box and the deck shape. Its rests_on (b119, b118) is a guess.
Step 41: ten Light Bluish Gray 1x2 jumper plates (one stud each) are laid end to end along the whole top of the bridge deck (b115-b121), forming the roadway.
The picture is small and the deck is made of several overlapping plates, so the rests_on lists are a rough guess, in order from the left end to the right end. The count of 10 is certain.

Step 42 (4x): four black 1x1 tiles with a clip (b132-b135) sit on the studs of the end jumper plates, two at the left end (b122, b123) and two at the right end (b130, b131) of the deck. They will hold the bridge arch bars later.
In the picture each clip sits on the single stud of one end jumper plate. The six jumper studs in the middle stay free.

Step 43: two black 1x2 handle plates (b136, b137) are clipped by their handle bars into the inner clip of each end pair on the deck (b133 at the left end, b134 at the right end), and stand upright. Two black 4L bars (b138, b139) are pushed into jumper studs and stand upright. They are drawn full size (1:1) in the callout.
The handle plates only hold on by the clip, so they rest on nothing and rests_on is []. The bars sit on the jumper studs b124 and b129, which I took from the picture.
The picture is small, so which jumper stud each bar uses is my best reading.

No new pieces on this page. The red arrows show the two handle plates (b136, b137) being tilted on their clips toward the upright bars (b138, b139), so each bar goes through the handle loop of its plate. The text beside is a fun fact about bridge paint, in three languages.
The picture is small. I took the join as a bar through the plate's handle loop. The bars stay joined to the jumper studs from step 43.

Step 45 (4x): four more upright bars (b140-b143) are pushed into the next four jumper studs along the deck (b125-b128), between the two bars from step 43. They make six hanger bars in a row, drawn full size (1:1) in the callout.

I recorded them as Black from the picture, like the step 43 bars, and as lego-30374 (4L). The parts list has only 4 black 30374, so the bar type or colour for some of the six may need checking. The picture does not show a different colour.

Steps 46-48 start the arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, made of several segments (shown in the top picture). This first segment is a black 1x4 tile held between two black 1x2 plates with a clip on the end.
Step 46: a black 1x2 plate with a horizontal clip (b144) is the first piece.
Step 47: a black 1x4 tile with groove (b145) is put on b144, with the tile sticking out past the clip end.

This page shows how to use the orange brick separator tool, with a QR code. It has no building step, so no pieces are added. The separator is not in the parts list, so I did not record it.
Step 1: a black 2x2 plate (b1) is the first piece.
Step 2: a black 1x6 plate (b2) is placed on b1. It hangs out sideways, with one end on the 2x2 plate. I could not tell from the small picture how many studs overlap, but it rests only on b1.
The overview picture at the top left shows the finished Sydney skyline model.
Step 3: a second black 2x2 plate (b3) goes at the same level as b1, beside it. The 1x6 plate b2 bridges b1 and b3 from above.
b3 goes under the already-placed b2, so it clutches nothing below it and rests_on is []. I could not edit b2's earlier entry, so I recorded the b2-on-b3 link as an other_join.
The picture is small, so the exact stud offsets are my best reading.
Step 4: a black 2x6 plate (b4) is added to the base, over the two 2x2 plates b1 and b3.
Step 5: a second black 2x6 plate (b5) is added, shifted sideways from b4 so the two overlap in a staggered layout. I read it as resting on b4 and on the 1x6 plate b2.
The pictures are small and the stud offsets are hard to read, so the exact rests_on lists for b4 and b5 are my best reading.
Step 6 (2x): two black 2x2 plates with two studs on the side (b6, b7) are added side by side at the right end of the base. Their side studs face the front.
I read both as sitting on the exposed studs at the end of the lower 2x6 plate b4. The picture is small, so this is my best reading.
Step 7: a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b8) is added at the front of the base, with its side studs facing front.
Step 8: a black 1x6 plate (b9) is added along the back edge, overhanging to the left.
The pictures are small, so the rests_on lists for b8 and b9 are my best reading of the layout.
Step 9: a black 2x6 plate (b10) is added at the left end of the base. It makes that end two studs wide.
The picture is small. I read it as a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795), not the one with side studs, and as resting on b9 and b4. This is my best reading.
Step 10: one more black 2x6 plate (b11) is added toward the right and back of the base.
The picture is small. The parts-list counts show it is a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795), because the 2x6 plates with side studs (lego-87609) did not drop. The rests_on list (b5, b8) is my best reading.
Step 11 (2x): two black 1x1 plates are added. The arrows point at one stud on the left plate (b10) and one stud toward the middle of the front of the base (b8).
The picture is small, so the exact studs they sit on are my best reading.
Step 12: a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b14) is added at the front-left of the base, with its side studs facing front.
I read it as resting on the left plate b10 and the 1x1 plate b12. The picture is small, so this is my best reading.

Step 13: a black 1x6 plate (b15) is added along the back-left edge, overhanging to the left. Two Dark Blue 1x2 plates (b16, b17) are placed on the middle of the base, as the first coloured pieces for the tower footprint.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.
Step 14: a black 6x6 plate (b18) is added at the left end of the base, forming the base of the tower area.
The picture is small, so which plates it sits on (b10, b14, b15) is my best reading.
Step 15: a black 2x6 plate (b19) is added next to the 6x6 plate, on the left part of the base.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b18, b14) is my best reading. I took it as a plain 2x6 plate (lego-3795) from the box icon.
Step 16: a black 1x6 plate (b20) is added along the back-left edge, sticking out to the left.
The picture is small. I read it as resting on b19, but I am not sure which plates it clutches.
Step 17: a second black 6x6 plate (b21) is added at the left end, widening the base on that side.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b18, b19, b20) is my best reading.
Step 18: a black 1x4 plate (b22) and a black 2x6 plate (b23) are added on the left end of the base.
The pictures are small, so where they sit is my best reading. The 2x6 shape in the box is black, and the parts list has no black 2x4, so I used a 2x6 plate (lego-3795).

Earlier, the parts-list counts after step 13 dropped White 1x2 plates (lego-3023) by 2 and left Dark Blue 1x2 unchanged. The picture showed blue plates, so I recorded b16 and b17 as Dark Blue. The colour of b16 and b17 may need checking.

Step 19 is a separate sub-assembly, built off the main base, and it will be attached to it later. The parts box lists a black 2x6 plate, a 1x6 plate, two 2x2 plates and two 2x2 plates with side studs. Only sub-steps 1 and 2 are on this page.
Sub-step 1: a black 2x2 plate (b24) is the first piece of the sub-assembly.
Sub-step 2: a black 1x6 plate (b25) is put on b24, overhanging to one side, the same way as b1 and b2 at the start.
The other parts in the box (2x6 plate, second 2x2 plate, two plates with side studs) are not placed on this page.

Sub-step 3: a second black 2x2 plate (b26) goes beside b24, under the 1x6 plate b25. It clutches nothing below, so rests_on is [] and the link to b25 is recorded as an other_join. This repeats steps 1-3 of the main build (b1, b2, b3).
Sub-step 4: a black 2x6 plate (b27) goes on top.
Sub-step 5 (2x): two black 2x2 plates with two studs on the side (b28, b29) are added at the front, side studs facing front.
The pictures are small, so the exact rests_on for b27, b28 and b29 are my best reading.
No new pieces on this page. The arrow shows the finished step 19 sub-assembly (b24, b25, b26, b27, b28, b29) being attached to the left end of the base.
The picture is small, so I could not tell exactly which base plates it clutches. I recorded one join (b27 with b21) to show the attachment. The sub-assembly may also clutch b23 and b18.
Step 20: a black 1x6 plate (b30), a black 1x4 plate (b31) and a Dark Blue 1x2 plate (b32) are added on the left part of the base, over the join with the step 19 sub-assembly.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of where they sit.
The parts list shows 1x6 plates dropping from 1 to 0 after this step and 1x4 plates dropping from 7 to 6, which matches b30 and b31.

Step 21 (2x): two black 1x4 plates (b33, b34) are added. Each sticks out sideways to the front of the base, turned so its long side runs front-to-back. One is at the left near the blue plate and one is toward the middle.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.

The parts-list counts dropped White 1x2 plates (lego-3023) again, 5 to 4, after step 20. That suggests the blue-looking 1x2 plates in steps 13 and 20 are counted as White in the inventory, not Dark Blue. I recorded them as Dark Blue from the picture, so b16, b17 and b32 may need checking.

Step 22 (2x): two black 2x6 plates with 4 side studs (b35, b36) are laid side by side across the front of the base, with their side studs facing front. They are held on the two 1x4 plates (b33, b34) from step 21 that stick out to the front.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.
Step 23: a Tan 2x4 tile with groove (b37) is laid on top of the front 2x6 plates b35 and b36. It spans both of them.
The picture is small, so exactly which studs it covers is my best reading.

Step 24: two black 1x8 tiles (b38, b39) and one black 1x4 tile (b40) are pressed sideways onto the rows of side studs along the front of the base. They rest on nothing from below, so rests_on is [] and the joins are recorded as other_joins.
Each 1x8 tile fits one group of 8 side studs: b8 + b6 + b7 on the right front, and b14 + b28 + b29 on the left front. The 1x4 tile fits the 4 side studs of b36.
The picture is small and I could not see exactly which side-stud rows are covered, so the joins are my best reading.
Step 25 is a small separate sub-assembly: the black 1x8 tile printed with 'Sydney', held on two black 1x4 plates. It will be attached to the base later.

Sub-step 2: the Sydney-print 1x8 tile (b42) is put on b41, with the tile sticking out to the left.

Step 26: a black 1x4 tile with groove (b44) is pressed sideways onto the left-front side studs. It rests on nothing from below, so rests_on is [] and the join is an other_join.
The picture is small. I took the studs it covers to be the 4 side studs of b14. The earlier step 24 tile b39 may cover a different set of studs than I recorded.
Step 27: a Dark Green 1x4 tile with groove (b45) is placed at the far right end of the base, on the back right corner. It is the first of the green pieces for the grass at the bridge end.
The picture is small, so which plates it covers (b11, b7) is my best reading.

Step 28: four Dark Green 1x1 tiles (b46-b49) go next to the green 1x4 tile b45 at the right end, to make a small grass area. A Tan 1x1 plate (b50) and a Tan 1x3 brick (b51) go beside it, as the base of the bridge tower.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of which base plates each piece sits on.

My earlier notes about colour mismatches were wrong. The unplaced-parts list seems to count down by part type, taking the first colour listed. So the colours I read from the pictures (blue, green, black) stay as recorded.
Step 29 (2x): two Dark Tan 1x2 tiles with groove (b52, b53) are placed at the right end of the base, next to the green tiles and the tan brick, to make the path or ground there.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.

Step 30: 31 Trans-Light Blue 1x2 tiles (b54-b84) cover the top of the base from the tan tile to the green and tan area at the right end, forming the harbour water. Two White 1x2 tiles with two vertical teeth (b85, b86) stand in the water as small sails.
The water tiles are in a strip about two studs wide, and the tiles have no studs, so nothing sits on top of them. The sail tiles therefore clutch base plates directly, in gaps left in the water.
The picture is small and the 31 tiles cover many plates, so the rests_on lists are only a rough guide, in order from left to right across the water. The count of 31 tiles and 2 sails is certain.
Step 31: two Dark Green 1x1 tiles (b87, b88) and a Tan 1x1 plate (b89) are added at the back-left end of the water strip, to make a small green bank with a stud for later pieces.
The picture is small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading of which plates they sit on.

Step 32: a Tan 1x3 brick (b90) is placed at the back-left end of the water strip. It sits on the Tan 1x1 plate b89 and on the base plate b4 beside it. It matches the tan brick at the right end (b51), the bridge towers.
The picture is small, so the rests_on list is my best reading.

Step 33: the left end of the base (the tower and Opera House ground) is covered with 4 Light Bluish Gray 1x4 tiles, 11 Light Bluish Gray 1x2 jumper plates (one stud each, showing as black dots) and 1 Tan 1x2 tile (b95) next to the tan brick b90.

The picture is small and these pieces cover many plates, so the rests_on lists are a rough guess based on the left-end base plates (b18, b19, b21, b23, b27, b30-b32, b10). The counts and types are certain.

Copy 1 is b107 (plate) with b108 (slope), at the left end. Copy 2 is b109 (plate) with b110 (slope), at the right end.
The picture is small, so which base plate each 1x1 plate sits on and which stud the slope shares with the tan brick are my best reading.

The picture is small, so which stud of each brick the stack sits on is my best reading.

The pictures are small, so the rests_on lists are my best reading.

The picture is small, so the rests_on list (b118, b115) is my best reading.
Step 40: a black 1x1 plate (b120) is pressed onto the left-end stud of the bridge deck (red arrow). A black 1x4 plate (b121), the last one, is added on the deck near that end.
The picture only shows the 1x1 plate arrow, so where the 1x4 plate goes is my best reading from the box and the deck shape. Its rests_on (b119, b118) is a guess.
Step 41: ten Light Bluish Gray 1x2 jumper plates (one stud each) are laid end to end along the whole top of the bridge deck (b115-b121), forming the roadway.
The picture is small and the deck is made of several overlapping plates, so the rests_on lists are a rough guess, in order from the left end to the right end. The count of 10 is certain.

Step 42 (4x): four black 1x1 tiles with a clip (b132-b135) sit on the studs of the end jumper plates, two at the left end (b122, b123) and two at the right end (b130, b131) of the deck. They will hold the bridge arch bars later.
In the picture each clip sits on the single stud of one end jumper plate. The six jumper studs in the middle stay free.

Step 43: two black 1x2 handle plates (b136, b137) are clipped by their handle bars into the inner clip of each end pair on the deck (b133 at the left end, b134 at the right end), and stand upright. Two black 4L bars (b138, b139) are pushed into jumper studs and stand upright. They are drawn full size (1:1) in the callout.
The handle plates only hold on by the clip, so they rest on nothing and rests_on is []. The bars sit on the jumper studs b124 and b129, which I took from the picture.
The picture is small, so which jumper stud each bar uses is my best reading.

No new pieces on this page. The red arrows show the two handle plates (b136, b137) being tilted on their clips toward the upright bars (b138, b139), so each bar goes through the handle loop of its plate. The text beside is a fun fact about bridge paint, in three languages.
The picture is small. I took the join as a bar through the plate's handle loop. The bars stay joined to the jumper studs from step 43.

Step 45 (4x): four more upright bars (b140-b143) are pushed into the next four jumper studs along the deck (b125-b128), between the two bars from step 43. They make six hanger bars in a row, drawn full size (1:1) in the callout.

I recorded them as Black from the picture, like the step 43 bars, and as lego-30374 (4L). The parts list has only 4 black 30374, so the bar type or colour for some of the six may need checking. The picture does not show a different colour.

Steps 46-48 start the arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, made of several segments (shown in the top picture). This first segment is a black 1x4 tile held between two black 1x2 plates with a clip on the end.
Step 46: a black 1x2 plate with a horizontal clip (b144) is the first piece.
Step 47: a black 1x4 tile with groove (b145) is put on b144, with the tile sticking out past the clip end.

Step 48: a second black clip plate (b146) is pushed under the other end of the tile. It clutches nothing below it, so rests_on is [] and its link to b145 is an other_join. The clip ends face opposite ways, so the segment can be hinged to its neighbours.
Steps 49 and 50 each build one more arch segment of the same kind as steps 46-48: a clip plate, a black 1x4 tile on it, then a second plate pushed under the other end of the tile.

Step 49: b147 (clip plate), b148 (tile), b149 (handle plate). The arrow then clips this segment onto the segment from steps 46-48 (b144-b146). Step 50: b150, b151 (tile), b152. The arrow then clips this third segment onto the second, so there are three segments in a hinged chain.

The boxes show two kinds of end plate (a horizontal clip plate and a handle plate). I used lego-63868 for b147, since the parts list shows only one left, and lego-60478 for the others. I could not tell which end of each segment joins which, so the hinge joins are my best reading.

Step 51: a fourth arch segment is built in three sub-steps, the same way as the others: end plate (b153), black 1x4 tile (b154), second end plate pushed under (b155). The arrow then clips it onto the chain, which now has four hinged segments, as in the picture.
The picture is small, so which end of this segment joins which end of the previous one (b155 to b150) is my best reading.

No new pieces on this page. The arrow shows the chain of four hinged arch segments (b144-b155) being clipped onto the free clip tile (b135) at the right end of the bridge deck. The chain stands up in the air, because it is not yet bent over to the left end.
The picture is small, so which end plate (b146) joins the clip is my best reading.

No new pieces on this page. The red arrow shows the arch chain bent over so that its free end clips onto the left clip tile (b132) of the deck. The arch now rises over the six hanger bars and hinge-leans against the two handle plates at the ends. The text beside is a fun fact about locomotives, in three languages.
